messages.text: Sefa studies Vell a moment — the tidy desk, the folded hands, the way he does not look at the clerk's empty stool — then says, "Three things, then, and we'll be on our way. How did Jassan Ferr die, and who found him? Who keeps the key to that room now? And has anyone else come asking after the strongbox — family, creditors, the Fist, anyone?" messages.name: Pell Dunmore
messages.text:
Pell leans an elbow on the counter, eyes drifting once to the tidied desk and back to Vell.

"A few things, since we're to do it clean. One — the room. Who holds the key now, the cooper or the landlord? Does he know we're coming, or do we need a word from you, in writing, so nobody shouts for the Fist when three strangers walk up his stairs?

"Two — the box. How big is it, what's it made of, and what's the seal — wax with your mark, a lead tag, something else? If I'm to carry a thing through a town of smiths unopened, I'd like to know it when I see it, and know if someone's already had a go at it.

"Three — Ferr. Three days dead. How did he die, and has anyone else been asking after his room? A clerk's ledgers don't usually need three hired blades to fetch. If there's someone else who wants that box, I'd rather hear it from you now than from them on the stairs."

He straightens. "Not arguing the price. Just the shape of the job."

messages.name: Bram Halloway
messages.text:
I settle the shield strap on my forearm, keeping my eyes on Vell.

“Seventy-five gold to carry a box across town. What trouble are you expecting—and how did Ferr die?”

I leave him room to answer, then add, “We’ll need a note with your signature authorising the collection. And tell us what the box and seal look like, so we bring you the right one.”

presses.text:
The die settles low — a ten — and against your three it makes thirteen, just short. Vell has been answering with the smooth, patient cadence of a man who has already decided what he will say. You watch for the pause before the last question, the shift of knuckle or breath.

"The box is ledger and letter," he says, still writing nothing, now pressing the note between his fingertips so the ink dries flat. "It holds what passed between this house and men who owe it. Creditors may well come when word of the death is known. None has come to me yet." He looks at each of you in turn, lingering nowhere, and when his eyes cross the empty stool they pass over it the way a man's eye passes over a room he has already left. "But the room is mine by right of business, and the papers are worth more than the door they sit behind. If one of them means to try his luck at the widow's latch, I would sooner have the thing under this roof."

The hammers run on outside, a bright, uneven ring, and through the shutter-light dust turns in the beam above the counter. Vell slides the note toward Bram, closes the inkwell and puts it back under the counter. "Now, the day," he says. "I will be here until you return."

opening.narration:
Beregost wakes to hammers. From every smithy along the street the ringing comes through the shutters of Ostrin Vell's counting-house, where the morning light falls on brass scales and rows of bound ledgers. Sefa Marrin, Pell Dunmore and Bram Halloway stand at the long counter. The three of you met here only this morning, and Vell has just hired you together.

Vell lays the terms out a second time, tapping the counter with one finger at each point. Jassan Ferr, his clerk, died three days ago in a rented room above the cooper's yard on the Coast Way. In that room is a locked strongbox of ledgers. Vell wants it here before nightfall today, unopened, with its seal whole. On delivery he will pay seventy-five gold for the three of you to share. Not a copper before.

Beside the counter stands a clerk's desk. Its stool is pushed neatly under it, the inkwell is capped and the blotter is clean, as if someone had tidied it and no one had sat there since. Vell does not look at it. He looks from Sefa to Pell to Bram, folds his hands on the counter and waits. "The Coast Way is not far, and the day will not wait for you. Is there anything you need to ask me before you go?"
